messages.subject: Learning to use Distance, I have a few questions
messages.subject_clean: Learning to use Distance, I have a few questions
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone, I am just learning to use Distance, as such this is my
first post to the listserver.  Hopefully this will work smoothly. I have
been playing around with the program for a few days now (versions 2.2
and 3.0) and have a few questions/problems.  Hopefully the answers to
these problems aren't too obvious or anything.

My first problem lies in the area of file management. That is, for some
reason I don't really understand how to save and call up files once I've
completed entering them.  I gather that the main commands with regards
to this are the assign and store commands, but when i try to assign
input to a file, I get the message stating that the file doesn't exist,
and when I've assigned output files they don't really seem to contain my
output.  That is, when I open the file, it  seems to a fresh Distance
environment with no input entered. Assign Log seems to work just fine.

Secondly how do you go back an edit a file if you have made an error
somewhere along the line? Do you have to edit through the log or record
file or something?

Thats all for now.  Hopefully, I've phrased my questions well enough
that they are understandable.  Please reply directly to my account,
chr...@alala.crc.si.edu.
Thanks for your help.

Chris

messages.subject: Question
messages.body_plain:
To display the output of an analysis, I have been using the list output
command. Is that the best way to do it? If so, the output is displayed
in Word Pad.  My problem is that all of my outputs, that is, even those
from analyses I've done in the past, seem to be appearing in this output
file, such that I have a string of old files with my new one added on to
the end. how do I remedy this situation? Am I doing something wrong?
Please reply to chr...@alala.crc.si.edu.

Thanks,
Chris

messages.subject: Announcement: Distance 3.5 released
messages.body_plain:
________________________________________________

            RESEARCH UNIT FOR WILDLIFE POPULATION ASSESSMENT
                            ANNOUNCEMENT
                     NEW SOFTWARE - DISTANCE 3.5
            ________________________________________________

Distance version 3.5 is now available for download via the world-wide web.

The web site address for download is:

              http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/

This site is also the new home page for program Distance.

Distance 3.5 is a new, fully windows-based update of the standard distance
sampling software Distance.  Distance provides an analysis of distance
sampling data to estimate density and abundance of a biological population.

The new software is a major update on previous versions.  It features a much
simplified point-and-click interface, with analyses displayed in a "live"
summary table, allowing interactive data modeling and model selection.
Several new features include the ability to select subsets of the data for
anlalysis, to import data from text files and to post-stratify on factors
such as age, sex, etc.  For a list of the new features, see the Distance home
page.

If you have any comments about the new program or the web pages, please
contact us at dist...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk.

 - Len Thomas
   Distance development project co-ordinator

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

messages.subject: Workshops: Distance sampling, Colorado 1999
messages.body_plain:
_____________________________________________

                    PRELIMINARY ANNOUNCEMENT
           TWO INTERNATIONAL DISTANCE SAMPLING WORKSHOPS
           _____________________________________________

          Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
                     University of St Andrews
                             and
             Colorado Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Unit

The Research Unit for Wildlife Population assessment announce two 4-day
training workshops in distance sampling, to be held in Fort Collins,
Colorado, USA in June 1999.  More information is given below.  Please contact
the workshop organizer (address below) to register interest and request
further details.

                      Workshop Information
                      --------------------

Title:        Design and Analysis of Distance Sampling Surveys

Instructors:  Steve Buckland, David Borchers, and Len Thomas
               (University of St Andrews)
              Bruce Lubow
               (Colorado Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Unit)

Dates:        Workshop 1: June 14 - 17
              Workshop 2: June 21 - 24
              (The program for both workshops is the same)

Venue:        Fort Collins, Colorado, USA

Cost:         TBA

Summary:

Distance sampling is the most widely used method for estimating the abundance
of wildlife populations.  The aim of these workshops is to train participants
in both the design and analysis of distance sampling surveys, including line
and point transects.  The workshops will be a blend of theory and practice,
and participants will learn the new, windows version of the software
Distance.  Participants are encouraged to bring their own data sets.  In the
latter part of the workshop, time is set aside for discussion of topics of
common interest in smaller, informal groups.

To register interest and request further details, please contact:

Rhona Rodger                   Tel:  +44 (0) 1334 463813
RUWPA                          Fax:  +44 (0) 1334 463748
Mathematical Institute
North Haugh                    e-mail:  rh...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk
St Andrews
Fife  KY16 9SS
Scotland
